assumptions: The calls the instrument wrote into the file.
limits: Reads the file's own calls; re-calling is call_bases_from_trace.
bio.jane/contract.question: What bases, qualities and trim bounds does this Sanger trace carry?

description: Read a Sanger trace (.ab1 / .scf / .ztr) from this project and hand its BASE CALLS onward as a record, with the per-base quality and the trim bounds beside them. This is what makes a sequencing read a pipeline input: verify it against a reference, align it, gate on its quality. The trace SIGNAL stays here — a record crosses a wire as bases, and a peak cannot be written as one.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

document.description: which trace file to read: its name (`read_F.ab1`) or its project file id. A file id is project-specific, so a template ships this unset.

min_quality.description: the mean phred a window must reach to be kept when trimming. Only applies when trim is true.

reverse_complement.description: read it on the other strand. A reverse primer's trace is the reverse complement of the strand you are verifying, and a name ending _R is the convention for it.

trim.description: emit the quality-trimmed read rather than the whole call list. The bounds are the sliding-window mean-phred bounds the chromatogram panel trims by, so panel and pipeline cut at the same base.

name: load_trace

ambiguous.description: how many calls are not A, C, G or T: the mixed positions

expectedAccuracy.description: the same number as a percentage of bases expected to be correct

meanQuality.description: the ARITHMETIC mean of the per-base phred, which is what FastQC plots. Always the higher of the two, because a phred score is a log of an error rate: keep it for comparison with other tools, gate on readQuality

qualities.description: per-base phred, parallel to the bases

qualityPlot.description: per-base phred as a plot along the read, with Q20 (1 error in 100) marked

readQuality.description: the read's own quality: the phred of its MEAN ERROR PROBABILITY, which is what seqkit's --avg-qual reports. Wire THIS into a gate to stop a bad read early

record.description: the read as a linear record, ready for any downstream step

sequence.description: its bases, trimmed when trimming is on

trace.description: what the FILE says about itself: format, instrument comments, call count, trim bounds. Not the signal, which cannot ride a wire
